exposure: Placental diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (IVIM) parameters (diffusion coefficient D, pseudodiffusion coefficient D*, perfusion fraction f)
outcome: Identification of false-positive small for gestational age (fpSGA)
Identification of true small for gestational age (SGA)
Differentiation between control, fpSGA, and SGA groups
cohort: The study included 28 control, 20 false-positive small for gestational age (fpSGA), and 27 small for gestational age (SGA) patients whose pregnancies were suspected to be complicated by SGA based on ultrasound biometries.
finding: Placental IVIM parameters (D, D*, and f) were significantly lower in the true SGA group compared to both control and fpSGA groups, with the perfusion fraction (f) being the most effective parameter for distinguishing true SGA from the other groups.
cross-section timing: Placentas were scanned at gestational weeks 28-41.
birth_weight: Estimated fetal weights <10th percentile were suspected as SGA, with final birth weight >10th percentile classifying fpSGA, and final birth weight <10th percentile classifying true SGA.
gest_age: Placentas were scanned between gestational weeks 28-41.
